live.name: MageCart
live.headline: MageCart: a threat actor listed in the MISP galaxy
live.in_short: MageCart is listed in the MISP galaxy catalogue. The record gives no aliases and no tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: MageCart is a threat actor named in the MISP galaxy catalogue.
The catalogue record lists no aliases and no tools for it.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: MageCart
next.headline: MageCart: card-skimming scripts planted on online checkout pages
next.in_short: MageCart is a name for web skimming: malicious JavaScript on checkout pages that copies card details. Reports from 2018 to 2025 describe many groups, thousands of sites and several large retail victims.

sentences.t: Malpedia describes Magecart as a malware framework meant to steal credit card information from compromised eCommerce websites.
Trend Micro says multiple groups use the Magecart code, which it describes as a piece of malicious JavaScript.
Headlines in Malpedia's reference list name Magecart Groups 4, 8 and 12, plus Keeper, Mirrorthief, ATMZOW and FIN6 in connection with Magecart skimming.
eSentire says FIN7 is one of many cyber gangs observed taking part in Magecart attacks.
WIRED reported in 2019 that Magecart hackers cast the widest possible net to find vulnerable ecommerce sites.
Trend Micro names Newegg and Ticketmaster among victims, and also online campus stores serving nearly 200 universities in the US and Canada.
A Malpedia reference headline reports campaigns that infected 311 restaurants through online ordering platforms.

ANY.RUN describes a campaign that mostly hit retail e-commerce sites, with victims in at least 12 countries, concentrated in Spain, France and the United States. It says banks, not merchants, bear the primary impact.
Malpedia says the first stage is typically JavaScript on a compromised checkout page, which relays card data to command and control servers.
Malwarebytes described skimmers where one injected line of code loads remote JavaScript on a shopping site. A fake iframe then overlays the payment form, and stolen data is sent back in encoded form.
Malwarebytes reported that Magecart actors registered free Heroku accounts to host skimmer infrastructure, and that it had earlier documented skimmers served from GitHub and Amazon S3.

Trend Micro lists three tactics: infecting third-party firms that supply code to other sites, scanning the internet for unsecured servers, and writing skimming code that works across many payment pages.

A report on the Volusion breach says most Magecart attacks use vulnerabilities in self-hosted stores to plant skimmer code. It also cites misconfigured cloud-hosting accounts in seven May 2019 incidents.
Sucuri says the ATMZOW skimmer is planted through Google Tag Manager containers. It uses base64 encoding and a long list of malicious domains hidden behind a firewall.
ANY.RUN describes checkout hijacking, imitation of payment pages and WebSocket-based theft of card data in a recent campaign.

RiskIQ reported that Magecart operators registered a lookalike domain on August 13th, 2018, and the skimmer on Newegg's payment page became active around August 14th. It was removed on September 18th.
RiskIQ said the Newegg skimmer code was recognisable from the British Airways incident.
WIRED reported in July 2019 that the group had hit 17,000 domains in a few months.
Trend Micro cited a separate attack in which 962 online stores were hit in 24 hours.
In October 2019, a report said hackers breached Volusion's cloud-hosted store infrastructure and that more than 6,500 stores were affected, possibly more.
In late 2023, Sucuri reported ATMZOW actors using 40 newly registered domains. After Google removed one container, the actors created new ones and reinfected sites.
ANY.RUN reported a campaign active for at least 24 months and supported by over 100 domains. It describes 17 WooCommerce sites, infected between February 2024 and April 2025, as likely linked to it.
Sucuri advises site owners to treat unexpected scripts on their pages as signs of compromise.
